title: Boot loaders
subtitle: From firmware to kernel — LILO, GRUB, and config paths

cards.front: Where the OS lives when the computer is off
cards.example: OS, apps, and data on disk
cards.notes: At power-on, RAM is empty — there is no OS in memory yet.

cards.meaning: CPU runs a small program from ROM (BIOS or UEFI) to find a disk and load something bigger into RAM
cards.notes: First step after power on in the boot chain.

cards.meaning: Small program that only loads other data and programs, which then run from RAM
cards.notes: First “real” program on disk that knows how to find and load the Linux kernel.

cards.meaning: Tiny first-stage loader loads a more capable second stage, which loads the kernel, which starts the OS
Power on → Firmware (BIOS/UEFI) → Boot loader → Kernel in RAM → init/systemd → user space
cards.notes: User space = your shell and services.

cards.meaning: LInux LOader — historical default on older Linux distributions
cards.example: older distros shipped LILO as standard
cards.notes: Older and less powerful than GRUB; originally no GUI menu for choosing OS/kernel. Rarely installed on new systems.

cards.meaning: LILO is older and less powerful; GRUB is easier to administer and common on modern servers
cards.example: almost every modern Linux server uses GRUB
cards.notes: Memory hook: LILO = old, simple, weak. GRUB = admin-friendly.

cards.meaning: GRand Unified Bootloader — what you see on almost every modern Linux server
Command-line interface, network boot, and MD5 passwords
cards.notes: Features called out in the topic notes.
If the course asks, answer with this and /etc/grub.conf.

cards.meaning: GRUB config path often a symlink into /boot

cards.notes: Course still wants the two grub.conf paths above if asked.
